subject: RFI: Burst-gradient, surge tolerance & fallback characterization for Zephyr Bank
messages:
From: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@zephyrbank.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@zephyrbank.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Burst-gradient / surge tolerance / graceful fallback evidence

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement diligence we're collecting a focused set of artifacts that demonstrate how Redwood handles sudden bursts (10x baseline QPS for short windows), progressive surge gradients (ramping over 30–60s), and the sequence of fallbacks when capacity is constrained. Specifically we need:

- A short description of the test methodology used to generate a burst-gradient matrix (including request size distributions, model variants, and KV/prefix cache settings).
- Empirical latency and throughput matrices (p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9) across the gradient and for different request token lengths.
- Clear documentation of fallback ordering (e.g., model variant fallback, cross-region, queueing) and evidence showing graceful degradation vs hard failures.
- Any soak or endurance runs you have that demonstrate recovery after sustained bursts.

If you can attach representative CSVs and a short readme, that would be ideal. We're aiming to finalize vendor selection in the next 3 weeks.

Regards,
Sarah Klein
Director, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Zephyr Bank

(Attachment: none)

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@zephyrbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Burst-gradient / surge tolerance / graceful fallback evidence

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear asks. We've compiled a concise package and a short methodology note below. High level summary first:

- Method: we run burst-gradient sweeps on a representative LLM family (open-weights variants we supply) across three sequence-length cohorts (short: <64 tokens, medium: 64–512, long: >512). We control for cold vs warmed KV cache by running warm-prefixed sessions and isolated cold starts.
- Observations: under a 10x instantaneous burst we maintain p50/p90 SLAs for short/medium requests via autoscaling + preemptible burst nodes; tail (p99.9) increases as expected but degrades gracefully — see attached matrix.
- Fallbacks: ordered as (1) autoscale burst, (2) model-variant fallback to lower-memory quantized variant, (3) route to dedicated spare pool in alternate region, (4) queued requests with SLA-based prioritization. Each step emits structured tracing and a metric tag for the event so you can correlate in logs.

Attachments included: redwood_burst_gradient_matrix_v1.csv (burst vs p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9), latency_tail_breakdown_90-99-999.pdf (visuals + interpretation), fallback-routing-sequence.txt (ordered sequence + decision thresholds), soak-test-logs-2026-09.zip (raw logs, anonymized request IDs).

Below is a concise methodology excerpt you can paste into your questionnaire: 

--- Methodology excerpt ---
Test harness: our in-house load generator (open-sourced harness available) that can shape traffic into step bursts, linear ramps, and exponential surges. All tests run against identical model checkpoints with kernel selection pinned for reproducibility.
Traffic profiles: baseline steady-state QPS (1x), then acute bursts at 5x and 10x that hold for 10s/30s/60s, and ramp gradients from 1x to 10x over 30s and 60s. For each profile we sample 100k requests across request-size cohorts.
Metrics captured: per-request latencies with token granularity, per-replica CPU/GPU utilization, KV/prefix cache hit ratio, autoscaler events, fallback triggers, queue lengths and drop/retry counts.
Failure injection: network partition (simulated 2s region hiccup), cold-start injection, and model-variant saturation (throttle one variant to force fallback).
Recovery criteria: 95% of replicas recovered to baseline throughput within 2x the ramp window; p99 tail falls to pre-burst within a configurable recovery window (default 5 min).
--- end excerpt ---

We can walk through the CSVs with your infra team — proposing a 45-minute technical review early next week. Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
(Attachment: redwood_burst_gradient_matrix_v1.csv; latency_tail_breakdown_90-99-999.pdf; fallback-routing-sequence.txt; soak-test-logs-2026-09.zip)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: internal: quick notes on numbers for Zephyr RFI

Looping in some quick empirical numbers to call out in the RFI summary (pulled from the attached CSV):

- Short requests (<64 tokens): baseline p50=18ms, p90=28ms, p95=34ms, p99=52ms, p99.9=110ms. Under 10x instantaneous burst (30s window): p50 shifts to 22ms, p90=45ms, p99=120ms, p99.9=370ms.
- Medium requests (64–512): baseline p50=48ms, p90=85ms, p95=120ms, p99=210ms, p99.9=620ms. Under 10x burst p99.9 peaks ~1.1s but we observe graceful degradation with no hard request failures when fallback sequence is enabled.
- Long requests (>512): tail amplification larger; p99.9 under 10x bursts frequently crosses 2.5–3s depending on KV cache warm status.

Notes: these numbers reflect tests where autoscaling + quantized-variant fallback were both enabled. When fallback is disabled we observed a higher rate (~0.8%) of 5xx errors from queue overflows in the synthetic harness for extreme bursts — we capture these in the logs.

I'll draft a short bullets summary for the external deck. Marissa — can you also pull the soak-run recovery graphs for the slide?

Ben
Principal Performance Engineer
(Attachment: reference to same CSVs + internal raw trace links)
